top.title: Think you have good eyesight? Try counting the stars in the Pleiades tonight
top.description: null Every autumn, I conduct an eyesight test that no reputable optometrist would understand. I go outside, find the Pleiades and count how many stars I can see. Usually I start confidently. One, two, three, four, five. Then things become contentious. Is that another star? Did I actually see it, or did I decide I ought to see it because I know it's there? I look away, look back and begin again. This is not, I should emphasize, a meaningful test of eye health. What it tests, rather, is how badly I've prepared for looking at the night sky. The Pleiades sit roughly 444 light-years away in Taurus and are right now becoming extremely convenient in the evening sky. You don't need a telescope to find them. You don't even need binoculars. In fact, you're likely to catch their collective brightness in your peripheral vision every time you go outside and look up. But every November the Pleiades remind me that naked-eye observing isn't as simple as opening the back door and looking up. How many Pleiades I can see can change depending on what I do during the next 10 minutes. What's happening and when to look You can easily see the Pleiades as a bright misty patch in your peripheral vision during winter. (Image credit: Haitong Yu via Getty Images) The Pleiades, also known as Messier 45 (M45) or the "Seven Sisters," are an open star cluster in Taurus. They're one of the closest clusters to the solar system and some of the youngest stars you can see with the naked eye — just 100 million years old. They're basically newborns. In mid-November, they rise in the east in the early evening and climb higher as the night progresses, making this an excellent time to get acquainted with them. Look east after dark for a tiny, compact group of stars. If you know Orion, which rises later, the Pleiades are above and to the right of it from mid-northern latitudes. Nearby you'll also find orange Aldebaran and the much broader V-shaped Hyades cluster. The Hyades are closer to the sun , but their stars are about 625 million years old. The name "Seven Sisters" creates an immediate observational trap: people assume they're supposed to see seven stars. That's not necessarily true. In fact, six is a common naked-eye result under decently dark conditions (note that the shape of the six brightest is like a mini Big Dipper /Plough), while people with sharp eyesight under darker skies may see more. The cluster itself contains about 1,000 stars. The number you personally distinguish depends on eyesight, sky brightness, atmospheric conditions and how well your eyes have adapted to darkness. That makes M45 much more interesting to me than a simple tick-box target. So tonight, don't just find the Pleiades — count them. He left over a decade ago on really bad terms, then when he returned to the industry with AEW five years ago — after many years away from it — that relationship also ended poorly. It has created an unexpected bond between him and the company’s head of creative, Triple H, after the two butted heads years ago. The idea of him retiring soon will surely disappoint many WWE fans since several other greats have ended their careers over the last few years. However, of the potential options to lead NXT, Punk is a fascinating choice. Obviously, he does not have experience running a promotion and TV show. But neither did Michaels, and he has done a very good job in the role. top.title: UTSA, basketball coach Austin Claunch part ways following DWI arrest
top.description: UTSA men's basketball coach Austin Claunch, center, watches his team during practice at the new Basketball & Volleyball Training Center in San Antonio on Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) UTSA and men's basketball coach Austin Claunch have mutually agreed to part ways, Roadrunners athletics director Lisa Campos announced Friday, ending his tenure after two seasons in the wake of an arrest on suspicion of DWI . Acting head coach Nick Bowman, a longtime Claunch assistant, will serve as interim head coach for the rest of the season after leading the Roadrunners to a 2-1 start. Austin Claunch, 36, is pictured in a mugshot at the Nueces County jail. He is charged with driving while intoxicated. (Courtesy of the Corpus Christi Police Department) "After thoughtful discussions about the future of the program, we mutually agreed that this was the right time for a transition," Campos said in a statement. "We thank Coach Claunch for his efforts over the last two years and wish him nothing but the best in the future. We look forward to this season with Nick Bowman at the helm." Less than a week before the start of the season, Claunch was found passed out behind the wheel of his Mercedes-Benz 350 Series at 2 a.m. on Oct. 27 in a Stripes parking lot in Corpus Christi, per the arrest report. The report from the Corpus Christi police department states that officers found Claunch unconscious, wearing his seatbelt with the vehicle running and the door left open. The initial call to law enforcement said Claunch had been "stumbling around" the store, and he responded with thick, slurred speech when the officers woke him. He admitted that he had been drinking and drove himself to the Stripes store, and he performed poorly on the field sobriety tests , per the arrest report. He refused blood and breath tests, and he was transported to an area hospital. His suspension was announced the next day, and the Roadrunners opened the season under Bowman's leadership on Nov. 2. "I want to thank our players, staff, administration, and fans for the support they've shown me during my time at UTSA," Claunch said in a statement Friday. "Dr. Campos and I agreed that it was best for both sides to move in a different direction. I want to thank Dr. Campos for the opportunity to coach at UTSA. I'll always be rooting for UTSA and the young men in this program." Because Claunch and UTSA mutually agreed to part ways, neither side is owed a buyout or any financial compensation, per a UTSA spokesperson. Claunch was hired in April 2024 on a five-year contract that ran through the 2028-29 season at an annual guaranteed compensation $550,000, and Claunch would have been owed 65% of his remaining guaranteed compensation if UTSA fired him without cause. Bowman came to UTSA as an assistant on Claunch's initial staff in April 2024 following a year as the lead assistant and recruiting coordinator at New Orleans. top.description: Pittsburgh Steelers defensive tackle Derrick Harmon isn't expected to return from a foot injury to face the Cincinnati Bengals ahead of their NFL Week 10 showdown on NBC's Sunday Night Football at Paycor Stadium, according to the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Ray Fittipaldo . Harmon hasn't played since suffering a foot injury Oct. 1 against Cleveland. Harmon was considered the Steelers' biggest question mark for Week 10 on the team's injury report . He was designated to return from injured reserve and practiced Thursday and Friday, but was limited. "We'll see by tomorrow," Harmon told reporters after Friday's practice. With 53 seconds left in the Bengals' 30-27 loss to the Steelers in Pittsburgh in Week 3, Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow fumbled as he was sacked by Harmon at the Pittsburgh 46-yard line. The ball was recovered by Pittsburgh's Sebastian Joseph-Day at the Cincinnati 49. Harmon beat Bengals offensive lineman Dalton Risner to get to Burrow. "We've got to be better," Burrow said after the game. "… You can't shoot yourself in the foot . Can't win in this league like that." Bengals tight ends Erick All Jr. and Tanner Hudson were adamant after the game that All recovered Burrow's fumble. All said a Pittsburgh player was just laying on the ball, but it was All who secured it. The call didn't go the Bengals' way. top.title: Germany U21 1-2 Belgium U21: Di Salvo's depleted side suffer first defeat of 2026
top.description: Germany U21 1-2 Belgium U21: Di Salvo's depleted side suffer first defeat of 2026 Due to players getting nominated for the senior side by Jürgen Klopp and many injuries, Germany looked very different from the side that played the majority of the qualification campaign for the European championship. However, they had the first two chances with Anton Kade's blocked effort and Paris Brunner's off-target shot. The next five minutes belonged to Belgium as Julian Duranville scored with his second attempt of the game. A minute after his solo effort narrowly missed the target, the former BVB winger had the simplest task of converting a tap-in after Lucas Stassin's cutback. Germany regained control after conceding the opening goal, with Muhammed Damar playing a big part in most of their promising attacks. The Wolfsburg midfielder was also the one who brought the hosts back in Essen twenty minutes before the half-time break. Lucas Noubi's challenge on Brunner gave Germany a free-kick opportunity from close range, which was calmly converted by Damar. The Hoffenheim loanee scored with the brilliant tactic of hitting it under the wall. The 22-year-old last played for Antonio Di Salvo's side a year ago, but he played a starring role in the absence of star names. Belgium's goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans saved his next attempt after a deflection as Damar decided to go alone in a 4 vs. 3 counter-attacking situation. Stassin hit the post with the last meaningful action of the first-half, although Germany were on top for the most part. It was Germany's turn to be denied by three woodwork early after the restart as the “Man of the Hour” Damar hit the crossbar moments before Kade's header narrowly missed the target. Damar and Kade created several promising opportunities in the final third, but they were among the first players to be taken off by Di Salvo. However, it was Belgium's substitute Romeo Vermant who scored within seconds of entering the game. Nicolo Tresoldi's Club Brugge teammate nutmegged Dennis Seimen to put the visitors ahead for the second time in the game. Brunner hit the sidenetting from a promising position before Brughmans made some decent saves to deny substitutes Maurice Krattenmacher and Merit Kömür. Debutant Louey Ben Farhat also came close to leveling the score for the hosts with his first action of the game. Nonetheless, Belgium U21 held on to their slender lead to beat their Germany counterparts for the third time in a row. After eight successive wins in the Euros qualifying campaign, Di Salvo's suffered their first defeat in 2026. Germany U21 will end the year with a friendly against Croatia in Rijeka on Tuesday.

top.title: Tinubu flags off $3.5bn Bakassi Deep Seaport construction
top.description: President Bola Tinubu on Friday flagged off the construction of the 3.5 billion dollar Bakassi Deep Seaport in Cross River. Tinubu, represented by the vice-president, Kashim Shettima, described the project as a historic economic intervention capable of transforming Nigeria’s maritime industry. Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony in Bakassi, Tinubu said the project would break a centuries-old jinx and reposition Cross River as a major commercial and maritime hub. “I have not come to Calabar to cut a ribbon and dance Ekpe Masquerade. I am here to break ground and break centuries-old jinx,” he said. He said the project would unlock Nigeria’s maritime potential, diversify the economy and demonstrate what collective commitment could achieve. The President said the seaport, supported by a proposed superhighway, would provide an evacuation corridor linking the South-South to other parts of the country. He said the concentration of more than 80 per cent of Nigeria’s foreign trade through Lagos ports had contributed to congestion, shipment delays and higher costs. “Lagos is not our enemy. Lagos is our elder brother in faith. No country eats with one hand. No country carries all its load on one shoulder. “When over 80 per cent of our foreign trade flows through Lagos, and Lagos alone, that is not strength. That is congestion,” he said. Tinubu said the Bakassi project would complement existing ports, improve cargo movement and strengthen Nigeria’s competitiveness in international trade. He said Nigeria accounted for more than 60 per cent of West Africa’s Gross Domestic Product but handled only 25 per cent of regional cargo traffic. The president said the country’s blue economy had the potential to generate 44 billion dollars annually. “The sea is no longer just water to look at. It is wealth to harvest,” he said. He said the project would create employment opportunities for engineers, crane operators, truck drivers, welders, customs officers, artisans and traders. Tinubu added that agricultural produce, including cocoa from Ikom and rice from Ogoja, alongside timber and solid minerals, would benefit from improved access to international markets. He urged Cross River residents to protect the project from political interference and misinformation. Earlier, Gov. Bassey Otu described the groundbreaking as a milestone in efforts to reposition Cross River as a major player in Nigeria’s maritime and blue economy. Otu said the project, initiated under his predecessor, Prof. Ben Ayade, had suffered political, administrative, legal and environmental setbacks. He thanked Tinubu for supporting the project and providing the necessary federal government approvals. The governor said the state had completed environmental impact assessments, hydrographic, geotechnical and geophysical surveys. top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Three races remain in the 2026 Formula 1 season, and for Aston Martin, the end of this disappointing season can’t come quickly enough. It has been a rough year for the Silverstone-based team, which had high hopes of competing amid the new regulations and the addition of legendary designer Adrian Newey, who took over as team principal. Unfortunately for Aston Martin and the Stroll family, it has been the team’s worst season since returning to the grid in 2021, with only seven points through 20 races. Aston Martin ranks 10th in the Constructors’ Championship, only ahead of Cadillac, which joined the Formula 1 grid as a brand new entrant this year. For many teams, upgrades and developments throughout a season address problems, but throughout the grand prix schedule, they have continued to be plagued with issues and have very few positives to take from the year. Aston Martin’s PU Problems Persist The problems started almost immediately, with the AMR26 suffering severe vibrations that forced Fernando Alonso to retire on Lap 21 of the Australian Grand Prix. Lance Stroll’s car had similar issues, and he eventually finished 15 laps down after limping around for data-gathering purposes. With Newey able to work on improving the aerodynamic side of the car, which ultimately led to a B-spec being introduced at the Hungarian Grand Prix, the main issue has primarily been reliability and power issues with the team’s Honda power unit. The team has struggled for pace all year, regularly finishing towards the back of the grid, and Stroll made recent comments on how much Aston Martin was losing compared to the rest of the field. “We’re really struggling on the engine side. We know that, so a lot of work to be done,” he told reporters before the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. “We’re missing two seconds [a lap] in engines, so it’s difficult.” With Alonso finishing qualifying in Malaysia two seconds behind pole sitter Max Verstappen, Stroll’s comments suggest that there is a lot more the car could offer if Honda’s power unit was on par with its competitors, such as Mercedes, Ferrari, and even Red Bull Powertrains. Throughout the year, Aston Martin have also struggled to see out races largely due to reliability issues, which have seen Alonso retire from seven races and Stroll retire from 13. Such issues have limited what either driver could do, with Alonso claiming all of the team’s points with a season-high P8 coming in Malaysia. Stroll, meanwhile, has had the worst of it and also achieved his best performance in Malaysia with a P12 finish, with just six race finishes. top.title: Estonia latest country to ban Russian athletes
top.description: Estonia shares a border with Russia [Getty Images] Estonia has become the latest country to say it will not allow Russian or Belarusian athletes to compete on its territory as a result of the ongoing war in Ukraine. It comes after Norway, Finland and Canada made similar announcements. The moves come amid a mounting backlash over the reinstatement of athletes from Russia and Belarus. In September, the International Ski Federation (FIS) relaxed its rules, saying competitors from the two countries would be granted access to its events "provided that they sign a declaration of neutrality". They had previously faced more stringent background checks on any voluntary link or paid duty with the military. Participation remains limited to individual events, with athletes banned from displaying national symbols such as flags, anthems or uniforms. However, it has now emerged that Estonia's government has written to the FIS, claiming that allowing entry to competitors from Russia and Belarus would undermine the country's support of Ukraine, and present an opportunity for propaganda. In a statement issued to BBC Sport, the FIS said it "is committed to offering full support to athletes, national ski associations and local organisers - with most of which we have a long-standing relationship - in the process of navigating what we know to be a very complex situation. "With that said, the Individual Neutral Athlete policy is clear in stating that notwithstanding eligibility, the host country visa and entry policies remain in place and are determined solely by the host country. FIS bears no responsibility for denial of visas or entry to any person granted eligibility under the FIS Individual Neutral Athlete Policy." On Thursday, Scandinavian neighbours Norway and Finland both said they would also block visas for Russian athletes because of the war in Ukraine. Norway is preparing to host the cross-country skiing World Cup next month, while Finland is due to stage the figure skating world championships in March. The International Skating Union (ISU) has said it "believes that athletes should not be punished for the actions of their governments in a world where, sadly, many conflicts are ongoing", and that it was "seeking clarifications" from officials in Finland. This comes in the wake of last month's decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) to overturn a ban of Russia by the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), a move condemned by the British, German, Finnish and Czech federations. Russia have been suspended from competing in IIHF events since the country invaded Ukraine in February 2022, but the Russian Ice Hockey Federation (RIHF) then successfully appealed that decision at Cas. top.title: How Kansas football coach Lance Leipold reacted to CFP expansion
top.description: LAWRENCE — Kansas football coach Lance Leipold shared his support for the expansion of the College Football Playoff this past Monday, Nov. 9, following the announcement that the postseason event would be moving to 24 teams with the 2027-28 season. Leipold, whose time in coaching includes competing in playoffs at Division III-level Wisconsin-Whitewater previously in his career, understands there are a lot of components to consider at the Division I level. That includes what’s going to happen with bowl games. But he thinks this can be a good thing for the sport, which currently has a 12-team playoff. Leipold pointed to the NFL and how it’s nowhere near as big a deal if the top team loses a regular-season game there as it is in college. From his perspective, college has to get used to the idea that teams will compete in the playoffs in the future with more losses than they’ve had in the past. It’s the new normal. RELATED: Kansas football coach Lance Leipold reflects on key play from UCF loss “All in all, I think it’s good for opportunities,” Leipold told reporters. “I think it’s great. I think we have to continue to manage the calendar as good as we can, for the sake of the game. But, yeah, I think it’s where it was going and as soon as it went to four, I knew it’d keep going. And will it get to 32? We shall see.” Leipold noted he didn’t think it’d be something that would diminish the regular season, as some have debated, as long as at least two rounds can be played on home fields and there isn’t too much of a turn toward neutral sites. The ability to have some level of home-field advantage as something to play for during the regular season is something he considers to be significant for any team and fan base. Also, the more the playoff expands, the more demand there is on programs and fans to travel and use more financial resources. The 24-team edition of the College Football Playoff is set to have 16 of its 23 games played on campus, with those matchups taking place during the first two rounds. The quarterfinals and semifinals will continue to be played at the College Football Playoff’s bowl partner locations. The first championship game of the 24-team format will be played in New Orleans in 2028. Jordan Guskey covers University of Kansas Athletics at The Topeka Capital-Journal. nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu on Friday flagged off the construction of the 3.5 billion dollar Bakassi Deep Seaport in Cross River. Tinubu, represented by the vice-president, Kashim Shettima, described the project as a historic economic intervention capable of transforming Nigeria’s maritime industry. Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony in Bakassi, Tinubu said the project would break a centuries-old jinx and reposition Cross River as a major commercial and maritime hub. “I have not come to Calabar to cut a ribbon and dance Ekpe Masquerade. He said the project would unlock Nigeria’s maritime potential, diversify the economy and demonstrate what collective commitment could achieve. The President said the seaport, supported by a proposed superhighway, would provide an evacuation corridor linking the South-South to other parts of the country. He said the concentration of more than 80 per cent of Nigeria’s foreign trade through Lagos ports had contributed to congestion, shipment delays and higher costs. “Lagos is not our enemy. Tinubu said the Bakassi project would complement existing ports, improve cargo movement and strengthen Nigeria’s competitiveness in international trade. He said Nigeria accounted for more than 60 per cent of West Africa’s Gross Domestic Product but handled only 25 per cent of regional cargo traffic. The president said the country’s blue economy had the potential to generate 44 billion dollars annually. “The sea is no longer just water to look at. It is wealth to harvest,” he said. He said the project would create employment opportunities for engineers, crane operators, truck drivers, welders, customs officers, artisans and traders. Tinubu added that agricultural produce, including cocoa from Ikom and rice from Ogoja, alongside timber and solid minerals, would benefit from improved access to international markets. nigeria.description: The Super Eagles of Nigeria bounced back to winning ways in their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, AFCON qualifying campaign with a 3-1 victory over Tanzania at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo on Friday. Chelle’s men maintained their two-goal cushion in the closing stages, although Arokodare missed an opportunity to complete his hat-trick. nigeria.title: Man United captain Bruno Fernandes rejects second contract offer
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has rejected the club’s second offer to extend his contract, leaving negotiations over the Portugal midfielder’s future unresolved. BBC Sport reports that Fernandes is out of contract at the end of the season, although United can extend his deal by 12 months, until 2028. The club wants to agree a new contract before using that option. If no agreement is reached, United are expected to trigger the extension before January 1. Without it, Fernandes would be able to sign a pre-contract agreement with foreign clubs from that date, with six months remaining on his deal. It is unclear when Fernandes rejected the offer. A resolution does not appear imminent amid the upheaval at Old Trafford: Michael Carrick was sacked on Thursday, while Mauricio Pochettino is expected to take over as head coach. United will hope Pochettino’s arrival can persuade Fernandes to stay. The midfielder came close to joining Pochettino’s Tottenham in 2019, before moving from Sporting to United six months later. He has scored six goals in 13 appearances for United this season. BBC chief football news reporter Simon Stone says Fernandes wants to compete for the biggest prizes and will want to see what impact Pochettino has at United. The club, meanwhile, must weigh the cost and length of a new deal against Fernandes’ recent drop in form after an outstanding previous season, when he broke the Premier League assists record and won major player-of-the-year awards. nigeria.title: U-23 AFCONQ: Nigeria suffer 2-0 defeat to DR Congo in first leg
nigeria.description: Nigeria’s hopes of qualifying for the 2027 Under-23 Africa Cup of Nations suffered a setback on Friday after the Olympic Eagles lost 2-0 to DR Congo in the first leg of their second-round qualifying tie. The Nigerian side, led by Ikorodu City head coach Bright Osehai Ozebagbe and former Nigeria U-20 assistant coach Deniran Ortega, struggled to convert their early opportunities as the hosts secured a comfortable advantage ahead of the return fixture. The coaching duo took charge in the absence of Super Eagles manager Eric Chelle, who was occupied with Nigeria’s senior national team preparations for their crucial Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Tanzania. Nigeria started brightly and nearly took the lead in the fourth minute when Victor Samuel’s effort missed the target. The midfielder had another opportunity five minutes later after finding himself one-on-one with the DR Congo goalkeeper but failed to convert. The missed chances proved costly as DR Congo took the lead in the 20th minute in controversial circumstances. Nigeria goalkeeper Samuel James appeared to have been fouled by a Congolese player while attempting to collect an aerial ball during the build-up to the opening goal. However, the referee allowed the goal to stand. The Olympic Eagles suffered another setback in the 30th minute when Brighton youngster Zadok Yohanna was forced off with an injury. DR Congo doubled their advantage five minutes before the break through Felozefe Mabete, who produced an impressive free-kick to put the hosts firmly in control. Despite their attempts to find a way back into the contest after the restart, Nigeria could not break down the Congolese defence, with the hosts protecting their two-goal advantage until the final whistle. The result leaves the Olympic Eagles with a difficult task in the second leg, as they must overturn the deficit to keep their qualification hopes alive. Nigeria will host DR Congo in the return fixture at the Remo Stars Stadium on Tuesday, where they will seek to secure an aggregate victory and advance to the final qualifying round. The Under-23 Africa Cup of Nations also serves as the qualification pathway for the men’s football tournament at the 2028 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles. nigeria.title: Boko Haram: Zulum announces ₦50k for each soldier deployed to Borno communities
nigeria.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Borno State Governor, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, has announced ₦50,000 support to each soldier preparing for deployment to the two communities of Maiwa and Koshebe villages. Our Correspondent report that Koshebe in November 28, 2020 came under massacre when some armed Boko Haram militants launched a devastating attack on peasant and laborer rice farmers working in the fields (near Zabarmari and Maiduguri), where over 100 farm laborers—many of whom traveled from Sokoto State in northwest Nigeria for seasonal harvest work—were rounded up, tied, and their throats slit. Likewise, in November, 2023, suspected Boko Haram insurgents again targeted rice farmers harvesting crops in the Karkut and Koshebe general areas of Mafa Local Government Area, killing at least 13 farmers and leaving others missing. But Zulum assured that he will provide the needed support to strengthen security along the Maiduguri–Mafa–Dikwa–Ngala highway, ensure safe travel, and revive trade in communities recovering from years of insurgency. The Governor gave the assurance on Friday during a visit to the headquarters of the 24 Task Force Brigade in Dikwa Local Government Area where he met with the Brigade Commander, Brigadier General Aminu Gumel. “My visit is primarily aimed at exploring measures to strengthen security along the strategic economic corridor, which connects Maiduguri to several communities in eastern Borno and serves as a vital route for trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities,” Zulum said. The highway links communities along the corridor to markets and facilitates the movement of agricultural produce, essential commodities and other goods. Zulum said improving security along the route would help residents travel safely, trade and rebuild their livelihoods. Addressing troops preparing for deployment to Maiwa and Koshebe villages, the governor pledged “to provide operational logistics and sustain welfare support. He announced ₦50,000 support to each soldier preparing for deployment to the two communities”. Governor Zulum’s administration has consistently supported military operations with logistics and welfare assistance as part of efforts to improve security and help displaced residents return to their communities. The Governor was accompanied on the visit by the member representing Monguno/Nganzai/Marte Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Engr Bukar Talba; member representing Dikwa Constituency in the State House of Assembly, Mohammed Zakariya; Commissioner for Information and Internal Security, Professor Usman Tar; Commissioner for Local Government and Emirate Affairs, Sugun Mai Mele; and other senior government officials. Justice Rahman Oshodi admitted the judgment as Exhibit L after overruling objections by Emefiele’s defence counsel. Emefiele is facing a 19-count charge bordering on alleged gratification, corrupt demands and abuse of office involving $4.5 billion and N2.8 billion. His co-defendant, Henry Omoile, is facing a three-count charge of alleged unlawful acceptance of gifts. Oshodi ruled that the certified true copy of the Supreme Court judgment was admissible as a public document. He said the fact that only the lead judgment was tendered did not render it incomplete or inadmissible. The judge also addressed concerns about the prosecution’s reliance on a civil judgment in the ongoing criminal trial. He, however, restricted its use to establishing what the Supreme Court had decided in the previous proceedings. He stressed that the judgment could not constitute evidence for or against any party in the ongoing trial. “It has been well settled that court judgments are only used when tendered in a trial to determine and confirm what was actually decided in the case. “They are not used as evidence given in them for or against any of the parties therein,” Oshodi said. The Director of Public Prosecutions of the Federation, Mr Rotimi Oyedepo (SAN), had tendered the document through EFCC investigator, Mr Alvan Gurumnaan. However, Emefiele’s lead counsel, Mr Ojo Olalekan (SAN), opposed its admissibility, arguing that only four justices signed the judgment. He maintained that Supreme Court decisions were ordinarily delivered by panels of five or seven justices. Ojo also argued that the judgment arose from non-conviction forfeiture proceedings and was irrelevant to the prosecution’s case. Counsel to Omoile, Mr Adeyinka Kotoye (SAN), aligned himself with the objections and urged the court to reject the document. Kotoye argued that admitting the judgment could undermine the principle of estoppel and the defendants’ presumption of innocence. He also questioned the prosecution’s decision to introduce the document after proceedings had begun. Responding, Oyedepo argued that the document was a duly certified Supreme Court decision admissible under Sections 102 and 104 of the Evidence Act. nigeria.title: Why I lied about having cancer – Blessing CEO
nigeria.description: By Wasiu Rokibat Nigerian social media personality Blessing Okoro, popularly known as Blessing CEO, has sparked fresh reactions after admitting that she falsely claimed to have breast cancer which in turn led to financial assistance from members of the public. The relationship influencer made the revelation during an interview with social media activist Martins Vincent Otse, better known as VeryDarkMan. Speaking during the interview, Blessing explained that although medical examinations discovered a lump in her breast, the result showed that it was not cancerous. However, she admitted that she deliberately presented the condition as cancer to attract sympathy from fans. In her words, “I do not have cancer. I had gone for a check-up and they found a lump in my breast, but it was not cancerous. I took advantage of that and told the public that the lump was cancerous. I played an emotional game.” According to her, she initially suggested that she might sell some of her personal belongings, including her car and house, before members of the public encouraged her to share her bank details for financial assistance. Blessing also disclosed that donations began coming in from different individuals but stopped after VeryDarkMan publicly questioned her cancer claims and demanded evidence of her diagnosis. “People had empathy, I did not come out to beg for funds. I played an emotional game. I wanted funds but I didn’t come out directly to ask for funds. I started with pretending I wanted to sell my personal belongings, my house, my car; It was fans who reached out to me in my DM, asking me to put out my account number; that’s when I put out my account number.” “The donation was rolling in, until VeryDarkMan came and say you people cannot be donating money for Blessing when there is no evidence. Immediately, VeryDarkMan made that video, the donation stopped. I am not proud of what I did.” The confession has renewed public attention to the controversy, which began in March 2026 when the influencer announced that she had breast cancer and appealed for financial support. She had previously acknowledged receiving about N13 million in donations but maintained that there had been confusion surrounding her medical condition. The matter also attracted the attention of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), which arraigned her over alleged offences connected to the fundraising campaign. nigeria.title: Jaji wins Zamfara APC rerun primary with 26,646 votes
nigeria.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto The incumbent member representing Kaura Namoda/Birnin Magaji Federal Constituency of Zamfara State in the House of Representatives, Hon. Aminu Sani Jaji, has won the All Progressives Congress (APC) court-ordered fresh primary election with 26,646 votes. Jaji defeated two other aspirants in the rerun conducted on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, to reclaim the party’s ticket after his earlier nomination was nullified by the Federal High Court in Abuja. The Chairman of the APC Electoral Committee for the exercise, Hon. Kabiru Idris, announced the results at the Kaura Namoda Collation Centre after the conclusion of voting and collation across the two local government areas. According to the committee, the constituency had 42,266 registered APC members, out of whom 27,389 were accredited, while 27,359 votes were recorded as total votes cast. Jaji’s closest challenger, Hassan Umar Dangaladima, polled 713 votes, while the third contestant, Musa Zubairu, failed to secure any vote. A breakdown of the results showed that Jaji won in both local government areas, polling 14,264 votes in Kaura Namoda against Dangaladima’s 465, while Zubairu scored zero. In Birnin Magaji, Jaji secured 12,382 votes, compared with Dangaladima’s 248 votes, while Zubairu again failed to record any vote. Declaring the results, Idris said Jaji had satisfied the requirements of the law, the APC Constitution and the party’s guidelines governing primary elections. “Having satisfied the requirements of the law, the APC Constitution and guidelines, I hereby declare Hon. Aminu Sani Jaji the winner of the fresh primary election,” he announced. The rerun followed a legal challenge instituted by Dangaladima at the Federal High Court in Abuja against Jaji’s earlier emergence as the party’s candidate for the constituency. The court nullified the earlier nomination and directed the APC to conduct a fresh primary within two weeks. The party’s national leadership subsequently fixed November 11, 2026, for the exercise in compliance with the court’s directive. Jaji, who is associated with the political camp of the Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle, has now secured the party’s ticket through the court-ordered process. The outcome settles the party’s immediate nomination contest in the constituency ahead of the 2027 general elections, following the legal dispute over its earlier primary election. nigeria.title: Malaysia arrests 53 Nigerians over immigration offences
nigeria.description: By Favour Ulebor & Agency Report No fewer than 53 Nigerians were among 112 undocumented African nationals arrested by Malaysian immigration authorities between January and October 31 over various immigration offences, Malaysian newspaper, Utusan Malaysia, has reported. The Nigerians recorded the highest number of arrests among the African nationals, followed by Uganda with 13, Kenya with 10 and Ghana with eight. The Director-General of Malaysia’s Immigration Department, Datuk Zakaria Shaaban, disclosed the figures in an interview with Utusan Malaysia, published on Friday. According to the report, other nationals arrested included Somalia (6), Tanzania (6), Senegal (4), Algeria (3), Burkina Faso (2), Togo (2) and The Gambia (2). One national each from Guinea, Zimbabwe and Libya was also arrested. Shaaban said the most common offence was entering or remaining in Malaysia without a valid pass or permit, contrary to Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63. He said 85 people were arrested for the offence, including 47 Nigerians. “The primary offence recorded is entering and remaining in the country without a valid pass or permit, under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63; this resulted in 85 arrests, 47 of which involved Nigerian nationals,” he said. The immigration chief said 23 others were arrested for overstaying their permitted period under Section 15(1)(c) of the same Act. He added that three people were detained for violating the conditions of their immigration passes under Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963. One Nigerian was also arrested for allegedly possessing forged documents under Section 56(1)(l) of the Immigration Act. The authorities also arrested an Algerian employer under Section 55B of the Act for allegedly employing foreign workers without valid immigration passes. Shaaban said the enforcement operations were part of efforts to curb undocumented migration and prosecute employers who engage or accommodate foreign nationals without proper immigration documents. “These ongoing enforcement operations reflect the authorities’ steadfast commitment to curbing the presence of undocumented migrants and taking firm action against any employers who harbor or employ them,” he said. However, the report did not disclose the identities of the Nigerians arrested or the specific locations where the arrests were made. nigeria.description: The Federal Government has signed a concession agreement for the Jeremiah Obafemi Awolowo International Airport, Port Harcourt, with PH Airport Limited, following assurances from the concessionaire that the arrangement would not lead to job losses. The Federal Government delegation was led by Keyamo, while PH Airport Limited was represented by its Group Managing Director, Eyo Asuquo. The signing followed a meeting between the minister and aviation union leaders to discuss the implications of the concession for airport workers. Speaking on behalf of the unions, Comrade Ben Nnabue said organised labour had approved the agreement after receiving assurances that no aviation worker would lose their job as a result of the arrangement. He said job security remained a major concern for the unions and that they were satisfied with the commitments made before endorsing the agreement. Also speaking, Asuquo highlighted Port Harcourt’s strategic importance in the Gulf of Guinea, describing the airport as a potential gateway for regional commerce, investment and connectivity. He said PH Airport Limited intended to improve the airport’s infrastructure and operational standards, adding that the concession would create more employment opportunities rather than result in job losses. According to him, the company’s vision extends beyond managing the facility to expanding airport-related activities, attracting investment and unlocking its economic potential. The Director-General of the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, Chris Najomo; Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, Olubunmi Kuku; ministry directors and aviation union leaders attended the event. The concession agreement was subsequently signed by the concessionaire and relevant ministry officials, with Keyamo presiding over the ceremony. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine President Trump Taps Two Democrats in Bipartisan Slate of SEC and CFTC Nominees as Both Agencies Run Short-Handed President Donald Trump sent the Senate four nominees for the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission on Thursday, his first picks for either agency in about a year and the first Democrats he has put forward for them. Former CFTC Commissioner Kristin Johnson, a Democrat, and Republican Steven Levine were nominated to the SEC. Republican Nathan Anonick and Democrat Matthew Rowland were nominated to the CFTC, Bloomberg Law reported. Each nominee needs Senate confirmation. The Senate Banking Committee will handle the SEC picks, while the Senate Agriculture Committee will take up the CFTC pair before any vote by the full chamber. Who the nominees are Levine was tapped for the SEC seat left by Hester Peirce, whose term expired, for a term running through June 5, 2030. He most recently served as general counsel and a senior adviser at the White House Council of Economic Advisers and previously worked at the SEC as counsel and deputy chief of staff to Commissioner Mark Uyeda. Peirce led the SEC’s Crypto Task Force and was one of the agency’s most vocal supporters of clearer crypto rules. Johnson would take the seat formerly held by Democrat Caroline Crenshaw, for a term ending June 5, 2029. She served as a CFTC commissioner until 2025 and is a former law school professor. During her time at the CFTC, she spoke often about digital assets, including custody and decentralized finance. Both CFTC nominees come from the Senate Agriculture Committee, which oversees the derivatives regulator. Anonick is legislative counsel to Chairman John Boozman and was a lead negotiator on the committee’s portion of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act. He was nominated to the seat once held by former Chairman Rostin Behnam, for a term ending June 19, 2031. Rowland is a CFTC attorney detailed to the committee who also worked on the Clarity Act and the committee’s 2024 crypto bill. He previously served on Johnson’s staff at the CFTC, according to his LinkedIn profile. He would fill the remainder of former Commissioner Summer Mersinger’s term, which expires April 13, 2028. entertainment.title: FWIFT 2026 Convention Communique: Industry Leaders Charge Women in Media to Embrace Cross-Border Growth
entertainment.description: The Forum for Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) successfully concluded its 2026 annual convention on Thursday, October 29, at the historic Glover Memorial Hall in Lagos, Nigeria. Convening under the theme “One Industry, Many Voices: Building Together,” the afternoon brought together over 200 practitioners from several sectors including; film, television, radio, advertising, and digital media to connect, share insights, and build mutual agency. Supported by the African Women’s Development Fund (AWDF) , the convention featured a keynote address by cultural curator Sandra Mbanefo Obiago , interactive panel sessions, break-out workshops, speed networking, and a flagship fireside chat titled “The Cross Over: A Career Beyond Borders.” The event drew leading voices from across the creative economy, including media executive Kadaria Ahmed , filmmaker Biodun Stephens, media personality Gbemi Olateru-Olagbegi, executive director Rosemary Egabor-Afolahan, and director Esosa Osagiede. Key takeaways and actionable resolutions from the convention sessions emphasized resilience, strategic partnerships, and structural evolution: Embrace Bold Collaboration and Risk-Taking: Speakers urged media professionals to shed apprehension around institutional partnerships. As highlighted during the panel discussions: “Do not allow fear of failing stop you from asking for help, do your due diligence on the people you want to partner with then go for it. If it does not work, do not stop, get up and go again.” Adaptability as a Survival Imperative: In an era of rapid technological and digital shifts across broadcast and film, participants were reminded of the absolute necessity of evolution: “If you don’t change with the times, you will grow stale.” Deconstructing Industry Myths: Addressing professional dynamics, panelists challenged antiquated narratives regarding female competition, affirming that systemic progress relies on solidarity: “Women work well with women, it is a myth that they do not.” FWIFT’s leadership noted that the conversations at Glover Memorial Hall mark a critical step toward cementing cross-sector alliances. The forum remains committed to translating these insights into actionable frameworks, mentorship programs, and policy advocacy for women shaping the future of African media. For more information on upcoming FWIFT initiatives, programs, and future events, visit the official website or follow @fwiftnigeria on social media. There is a lot that goes into establishing a successful business. It requires developing the business idea, securing clients, building a customer base and eventually bringing people on board. Starting a business and watching it grow can be an exciting experience. However, one thing many start-up founders overlook is the importance of having the right organisational structure in place. It is one thing to have a great business idea and attract talented employees, but it is another thing to create an environment where everyone understands their responsibilities, knows who they report to and can work effectively towards achieving the company’s objectives. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. As part of the recruitment process, the first thing I ensured was that a manager was hired before proceeding to fill the remaining vacancies. The idea was simple. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. During the recruitment process, I clearly communicated each employee’s responsibilities and the person they would be reporting to. These details were also stated in their respective offer letters, so everyone understood their roles and the management structure they were expected to work within. However, there was a challenge. Before the manager was hired, an accountant who was personally known to both co-founders had also been in charge of the previous employees. Following the restructuring, the founders had communicated their desire for a new operational arrangement, and this was clearly reflected in the recruitment brief. Although the new employees understood that they were expected to report to the newly hired manager, the existing employees still had their loyalty to the accountant, who had previously been in charge. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. It offers viewers a chance to see beyond the familiar celebrity image and learn more about the person behind it. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) UTSA and men's basketball coach Austin Claunch have mutually agreed to part ways, Roadrunners athletics director Lisa Campos announced Friday, ending his tenure after two seasons in the wake of an arrest on suspicion of DWI . Acting head coach Nick Bowman, a longtime Claunch assistant, will serve as interim head coach for the rest of the season after leading the Roadrunners to a 2-1 start. "We thank Coach Claunch for his efforts over the last two years and wish him nothing but the best in the future. We look forward to this season with Nick Bowman at the helm." Less than a week before the start of the season, Claunch was found passed out behind the wheel of his Mercedes-Benz 350 Series at 2 a.m. on Oct. 27 in a Stripes parking lot in Corpus Christi, per the arrest report. The report from the Corpus Christi police department states that officers found Claunch unconscious, wearing his seatbelt with the vehicle running and the door left open. The initial call to law enforcement said Claunch had been "stumbling around" the store, and he responded with thick, slurred speech when the officers woke him. He admitted that he had been drinking and drove himself to the Stripes store, and he performed poorly on the field sobriety tests , per the arrest report. "I want to thank our players, staff, administration, and fans for the support they've shown me during my time at UTSA," Claunch said in a statement Friday. I'll always be rooting for UTSA and the young men in this program." sports.description: Germany U21 1-2 Belgium U21: Di Salvo's depleted side suffer first defeat of 2026 Due to players getting nominated for the senior side by Jürgen Klopp and many injuries, Germany looked very different from the side that played the majority of the qualification campaign for the European championship. However, they had the first two chances with Anton Kade's blocked effort and Paris Brunner's off-target shot. The next five minutes belonged to Belgium as Julian Duranville scored with his second attempt of the game. A minute after his solo effort narrowly missed the target, the former BVB winger had the simplest task of converting a tap-in after Lucas Stassin's cutback. Germany regained control after conceding the opening goal, with Muhammed Damar playing a big part in most of their promising attacks. The Wolfsburg midfielder was also the one who brought the hosts back in Essen twenty minutes before the half-time break. Lucas Noubi's challenge on Brunner gave Germany a free-kick opportunity from close range, which was calmly converted by Damar. The Hoffenheim loanee scored with the brilliant tactic of hitting it under the wall. The 22-year-old last played for Antonio Di Salvo's side a year ago, but he played a starring role in the absence of star names. Belgium's goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans saved his next attempt after a deflection as Damar decided to go alone in a 4 vs. 3 counter-attacking situation. Stassin hit the post with the last meaningful action of the first-half, although Germany were on top for the most part. It was Germany's turn to be denied by three woodwork early after the restart as the “Man of the Hour” Damar hit the crossbar moments before Kade's header narrowly missed the target. Damar and Kade created several promising opportunities in the final third, but they were among the first players to be taken off by Di Salvo. However, it was Belgium's substitute Romeo Vermant who scored within seconds of entering the game. Nicolo Tresoldi's Club Brugge teammate nutmegged Dennis Seimen to put the visitors ahead for the second time in the game. Brunner hit the sidenetting from a promising position before Brughmans made some decent saves to deny substitutes Maurice Krattenmacher and Merit Kömür. Debutant Louey Ben Farhat also came close to leveling the score for the hosts with his first action of the game. Nonetheless, Belgium U21 held on to their slender lead to beat their Germany counterparts for the third time in a row. After eight successive wins in the Euros qualifying campaign, Di Salvo's suffered their first defeat in 2026. Germany U21 will end the year with a friendly against Croatia in Rijeka on Tuesday.

sports.title: Estonia latest country to ban Russian athletes
sports.description: Estonia shares a border with Russia [Getty Images] Estonia has become the latest country to say it will not allow Russian or Belarusian athletes to compete on its territory as a result of the ongoing war in Ukraine. It comes after Norway, Finland and Canada made similar announcements. The moves come amid a mounting backlash over the reinstatement of athletes from Russia and Belarus. In September, the International Ski Federation (FIS) relaxed its rules, saying competitors from the two countries would be granted access to its events "provided that they sign a declaration of neutrality". They had previously faced more stringent background checks on any voluntary link or paid duty with the military. Participation remains limited to individual events, with athletes banned from displaying national symbols such as flags, anthems or uniforms. However, it has now emerged that Estonia's government has written to the FIS, claiming that allowing entry to competitors from Russia and Belarus would undermine the country's support of Ukraine, and present an opportunity for propaganda. In a statement issued to BBC Sport, the FIS said it "is committed to offering full support to athletes, national ski associations and local organisers - with most of which we have a long-standing relationship - in the process of navigating what we know to be a very complex situation. "With that said, the Individual Neutral Athlete policy is clear in stating that notwithstanding eligibility, the host country visa and entry policies remain in place and are determined solely by the host country. FIS bears no responsibility for denial of visas or entry to any person granted eligibility under the FIS Individual Neutral Athlete Policy." On Thursday, Scandinavian neighbours Norway and Finland both said they would also block visas for Russian athletes because of the war in Ukraine. Norway is preparing to host the cross-country skiing World Cup next month, while Finland is due to stage the figure skating world championships in March. The International Skating Union (ISU) has said it "believes that athletes should not be punished for the actions of their governments in a world where, sadly, many conflicts are ongoing", and that it was "seeking clarifications" from officials in Finland. This comes in the wake of last month's decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) to overturn a ban of Russia by the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), a move condemned by the British, German, Finnish and Czech federations. Russia have been suspended from competing in IIHF events since the country invaded Ukraine in February 2022, but the Russian Ice Hockey Federation (RIHF) then successfully appealed that decision at Cas. The court said that IIHF arguments citing safety and security were "not supported by sufficient evidence", but the Hockey Federation of Ukraine said the ruling caused "special outrage". sports.title: How Kansas football coach Lance Leipold reacted to CFP expansion
sports.description: LAWRENCE — Kansas football coach Lance Leipold shared his support for the expansion of the College Football Playoff this past Monday, Nov. 9, following the announcement that the postseason event would be moving to 24 teams with the 2027-28 season. Leipold, whose time in coaching includes competing in playoffs at Division III-level Wisconsin-Whitewater previously in his career, understands there are a lot of components to consider at the Division I level. That includes what’s going to happen with bowl games. But he thinks this can be a good thing for the sport, which currently has a 12-team playoff. Leipold pointed to the NFL and how it’s nowhere near as big a deal if the top team loses a regular-season game there as it is in college. From his perspective, college has to get used to the idea that teams will compete in the playoffs in the future with more losses than they’ve had in the past. It’s the new normal. RELATED: Kansas football coach Lance Leipold reflects on key play from UCF loss “All in all, I think it’s good for opportunities,” Leipold told reporters. “I think it’s great. I think we have to continue to manage the calendar as good as we can, for the sake of the game. But, yeah, I think it’s where it was going and as soon as it went to four, I knew it’d keep going. And will it get to 32? We shall see.” Leipold noted he didn’t think it’d be something that would diminish the regular season, as some have debated, as long as at least two rounds can be played on home fields and there isn’t too much of a turn toward neutral sites. The ability to have some level of home-field advantage as something to play for during the regular season is something he considers to be significant for any team and fan base. Also, the more the playoff expands, the more demand there is on programs and fans to travel and use more financial resources. The 24-team edition of the College Football Playoff is set to have 16 of its 23 games played on campus, with those matchups taking place during the first two rounds. The quarterfinals and semifinals will continue to be played at the College Football Playoff’s bowl partner locations. The first championship game of the 24-team format will be played in New Orleans in 2028. Jordan Guskey covers University of Kansas Athletics at The Topeka Capital-Journal. sports.title: Manchester United confirm new head coach ahead of Liverpool clash
sports.description: Manchester United confirm new head coach ahead of Liverpool clash Mauricio Pochettino Faces Liverpool Test as Manchester United Reset Begins Manchester United have done what desperate clubs do when results collapse and the table starts to look ugly. They have changed the manager. Mauricio Pochettino is in, Michael Carrick is out, and his first proper problem arrives immediately, Liverpool at Anfield. There is no gentle introduction here. United are 18th, they have eight points from 10 league games, and the numbers under Carrick were heading in one direction. His last game summed it up, a chaotic 4-4 draw at home to Aston Villa in which United needed two stoppage-time goals just to scrape a point. Entertaining, maybe. Sustainable, clearly not. Pochettino appointment made at speed United confirmed Pochettino on Friday, one day after Carrick was dismissed. He has signed a deal running until the summer of 2029, with the club reportedly paying around £7.4 million to release him from his contract with the United States national team. The pitch from United is familiar enough. High-intensity football, attacking ideas, young players improving. All well and good, but right now this is about stabilising a side that has won only three of 15 matches in all competitions this season, with just one league victory. Pochettino returns to English football after spells at Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea. His CV in England remains respectable rather than glittering. He reached the League Cup and Champions League finals with Tottenham, but did not win either. At Paris Saint-Germain, he did at least collect Ligue 1 and the French Cup. Anfield comes too soon for comfort Timing matters, and for United this timing is awkward. Pochettino will first oversee the United States in Concacaf Nations League quarter-final matches against Haiti on November 14 and 17. He then begins officially at Old Trafford on Wednesday, meets the squad, runs training on Thursday and has three days to prepare for Liverpool on Sunday, November 22. That is barely enough time to learn names, never mind install a system. He will have to rely on clarity and simplicity. Organise the team, tighten the distances, stop the chaos. Anything more sophisticated can wait. Carrick exit reflects deeper problems Carrick’s dismissal ends a brief reign that never gained traction. He had taken over in January after Ruben Amorim’s departure and earned a full-time deal after securing Champions League qualification. Since then, the drop has been severe. Fifteen matches into a two-year contract signed in May, he is gone. The only league win came in a 5-2 result against Ipswich on August 30. Everything else left United drifting towards the bottom three. That is why Pochettino has been hired. Not for sentiment, not for long-term theory, but because United need points, structure and credibility, starting at Anfield.

sports.title: One single matchup that gives Michigan some hope against Oregon
sports.description: Not much has gone right for Michigan this college football season. So little that head coach Kyle Whittingham could suddenly find himself on the chopping block when all is said and done after just one year. Heading into a road test against resurgent Oregon, the Wolverines could be headed for yet more disaster. But one matchup on the field might give them a fighting chance. Strength vs. strength Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola celebrates a touchdown by Oregon running back Dierre Hill Jr. as the Oregon Ducks face the USC Trojans on Sept. 26, 2026, at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum in Los Angeles, California. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Oregon enters its Saturday showdown as a 10.5-point favorite, but Michigan has one significant matchup advantage that could make this considerably more competitive: its elite pass defense against Oregon’s passing attack. The Wolverines are allowing just 154.8 passing yards per game, ranking fourth nationally. They have also surrendered only eight passing touchdowns this season. For an Oregon offense averaging 285.4 passing yards per game, sitting top 15 in FBS, that represents a credible challenge. Pressure without blitzing Michigan’s defensive front makes this matchup particularly dangerous. The Wolverines have recorded 21 sacks and 53 tackles for loss, demonstrating their ability to disrupt quarterbacks before routes develop. Defensive lineman John Henry Daley leads the team with six sacks and nine tackles for loss. If he consistently wins his individual battles against Oregon’s blockers, quarterback Dylan Raiola could face uncomfortable decisions and hurried throws. That matters because Raiola has thrown for 1,354 yards, 11 touchdowns and just two interceptions. Protecting that efficiency against Michigan’s pressure will be essential. More: Predicting Big Ten football scores for Week 11’s biggest games Numbers favor Michigan’s defense The contrast is striking. Oregon is a potent aerial offense, while Michigan ranks fourth nationally in total defense, surrendering only 255.3 yards per game on average. Michigan also has veteran defensive backs capable of challenging Oregon’s receivers in man coverage. Will that be enough? Almost certainly not, considering Michigan basically can’t move the ball. But the Wolverines’ pass rush and secondary present a legitimate opportunity early on. That could theoretically slow down the Ducks’ aerial attack enough to make it close. sports.title: Tiger Woods remembers Dan Hicks after unexpected death: ‘A great friend to me’
sports.description: Tiger Woods paid tribute to late NBC Sports golf voice Dan Hicks , calling the longtime broadcaster "a great friend to me both on and off the course" following Hicks' unexpected death at 64. "Dan Hicks was beloved by all who had the privilege of knowing and working alongside him," Woods said in a statement mourning Hicks, who died Nov. 11 as a result of an acute illness. "His kindness, warmth, and presence will be deeply missed. Like so many in the golf world, Dan was a great friend to me both on and off the course. I had the utmost respect for him and the incredible job he did for our sport for decades." For more than a quarter-century, Hicks was the defining soundtrack to Woods' career, calling 27 of his PGA Tour victories — including Woods' iconic 12-foot birdie putt on the 72nd hole at Torrey Pines to force a playoff at the 2008 U.S. Open , punctuated by Hicks' timeless call: "Expect anything different?" "Our thoughts are with Hannah and their daughters during this incredibly difficult time," Woods added, referring to Hicks' wife, fellow broadcaster Hannah Storm, and their three daughters, Hannah, Ellery, and Riley. "I hope they find comfort in knowing how much he meant to so many people and the lasting impact he made on everyone whose life he touched." View this post on Instagram Storm announced her husband's passing on social media , remembering him as "truly one of a kind and, quite simply, the person everyone wanted to be around." Born and raised in Tucson, Arizona, Hicks graduated from Sabino High School and the University of Arizona before starting in local radio and television. After joining CNN in 1989 and moving to NBC Sports in 1992, he worked as a tower announcer until being named lead golf play-by-play voice in 2000. Beyond anchoring NBC's coverage of the U.S. Open, The Open Championship , Ryder Cup, Presidents Cup and FedEx Cup Playoffs, Hicks was a versatile fixture across sports — calling Olympic swimming and skiing, including the U.S. men's freestyle relay comeback at the 2008 Beijing Games, and returning as the lead voice for Notre Dame Football in 2024. technology.description: How do you think you're going to die? If you go by the current statistics for deaths in the US , it's reasonable to expect that cancer or heart disease will eventually get you. But OpenAI Foundation board member and Alignment Research Center Executive Director Paul Cristiano thinks we should all be worried about another major mortality risk. Speaking at a lecture series this week , Cristiano bluntly told the audience in a Toronto Convention Center, "I think for most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident." In the opening lecture of a three-part series , Cristiano outlined his worries about the risk of an impending "AI takeover." He defined that as a situation where goal-pursuing AI systems "call the shots in the same sense that humans today call the shots and what happens on Earth" and where any human trying to stop them "would be as ineffective as if you or me was trying to stop the US military." technology.title: Mozilla leaves Solo website owners to go it alone as hosting shuts down
technology.description: Solo, Mozilla's LLM-powered website builder and hosting service, is shutting down. All sites and data will be deleted on November 30. Mozilla launched Solo in December 2023 as a "Mozilla Innovation Project," aimed at helping sole traders to build themselves a webpage for their services. S ome 54,000 people used its LLM to build pages, and relied on Mozilla to host them – complete with custom domain names. Well, not any more. Now the Soloist.ai homepage says: "We've made the difficult decision to close Solo. We have appreciated all of your support building and growing this product, and the feedback we've received from all of you. Solo will cease operations on Nov 30, 2026." Users now have just over two weeks left to find a new home for their pages, although Mozilla says it first notified them on October 1. According to the support FAQ , users can download a ZIP containing an HTML export, contact form and newsletter submissions, and a CSV linking to their images. The images themselves must be downloaded separately. Domains purchased through Solo Domains must also be moved to Name.com , with Mozilla handling the transfer after users create an account and supply its code. So much for having the fiddly bits taken care of. It also points at a couple of other bot-based site-generating services – in case all this feels like a bit too much. We suspect that for the sort of technophobes that this was aimed at, it very probably will. Mozilla told The Register : "Experimentation is an important part of Mozilla's mission to make the internet better and give people more choice and control online. Sometimes, that means making the decision to bring a product to an end. Solo will officially shut down on November 30, 2026. We initially notified customers on October 1, providing a 60-day transition period, and have been offering support to help them download their website data and migrate their domains purchased via Solo Domains to another hosting provider." It seems that some 54,000 users were not enough to keep it going, and we can see that this would cost money to keep running. An HTML export is a start, though the FAQ doesn't explain how much work it will take to get a complete, functioning site running elsewhere. Buried in the dark recesses of the web is this vulture's own nearly 30-year-old homepage, created using a mixture of Claris Home Page (which was excellent) and Microsoft FrontPage (ever so slightly less so). We saw what a mess machine-generated web content was back then, and thanks to LLMs, we suspect it is almost infinitely worse now. Mozilla might have made a few bucks by finding a commercial partner to take on its users, and perhaps through them offer a paid site-and-domain transfer service. technology.title: Email addresses used in European school bomb hoaxes spotted in old infostealer logs
technology.description: Two email addresses used to send bomb threats that disrupted thousands of Italian schools this week were found exposed in infostealer logs for over a year, experts say. Researchers at Hudson Rock looked into the two university email addresses used to send the bomb threats. One, from Egypt’s Kafrelsheikh University, was scooped up by Vidar – a cybercrime tool that steals saved account credentials and passwords from an infected computer and leaks them to attackers – as far back as October 2021. The other, from Taiwan's Dayeh University, was found among the 284 million addresses included in the massive AlienTXTBASE infostealer dump , dated February 2025. The experts said that the two addresses in infostealer logs do not strictly mean that those behind the bomb threats gained access to the accounts using the previous infostealer compromise. However, it suggests that there was ample time for the universities and Microsoft, which both universities used for authentication, to take action against the accounts that they should have been aware were appearing in infostealer logs. Modern threat intelligence has made infostealer logs highly visible. "Both findings place credential exposure well before the disruption, creating a substantial window in which exposed access could have been investigated and secured," Hudson Rock said . The researchers said that they would need access to details such as the email headers, and data from email providers, including sign-in events and audit records, that could show them more about who sent the email and from what session. Understanding whether the sender authenticated into the account could rule out spoofing, but would not in itself provide proof that the sender used a corresponding password taken from an infostealer log, Hudson Rock noted. There are many ways to get around password-based authentication . The researchers said that in any case where a credential is detected among infostealer logs, the organizations responsible for those accounts must contain them, revoke their access, rotate secrets, and go looking for suspicious activity. "The disruption illustrates why credential exposure deserves attention beyond fraud and data theft," the researchers said. "An account associated with an ordinary university user can become a means of reaching schools, frightening families, and consuming emergency resources." The threats Around 6,300 of Italy's 7,476 state schools received fake bomb threat emails between November 11-12, although only around 390 of them evacuated their respective buildings. The emails contained messaging such as "we will annihilate you," and "we will carry out genocide against Italians," and mention of a "powerful explosive device… with a remote trigger."
